summary: Defines an extensible message format for responses to message tracking requests. Tracking is used along with delivery status and message disposition notifications, usually when one of them has not arrived in a reasonable time.

eli5.summary: When you ask where your package is, the answer has to come in a standard form. This document defines that form.

questions: what do the tracking action values mean
subtitle: The MIME format a mail server uses to report where a tracked message currently is.

tldr.problem: When a sender asks where a message went, the answer needs a standard, machine-readable form that works across servers.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 3886 defines the message/tracking-status MIME type, modeled on the delivery status format of RFC 3464, with per-message fields followed by groups of per-recipient fields, including an Action field with seven values.
tldr.outcome: Servers can report whether a message failed, is queued, was delivered, expanded, relayed, transferred or is opaque, and tracking agents know when to keep asking further downstream. The RFC updates RFC 3463.

today: RFC 3886 is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 3463. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Introduction and Role
sections.content:
Message tracking is used to find the status of undelivered email on request. It works alongside Delivery Status Notifications (DSNs) and Message Disposition Notifications (MDNs, RFC 3798). A tracking request is normally issued only when neither has arrived within a reasonable time.

RFC 3886 defines only the format of the status information, in the same spirit as RFC 3464. It is sent in response to a request under the Message Tracking Query Protocol (RFC 3887). Labeling messages for tracking is done by an SMTP extension in RFC 3885.

The document is based on RFC 3464 and includes some of its sections by reference: terminology, general conventions for fields, the *-type subfields and the lexical tokens imported from RFC 822.
sections.eli5: This document does not do the tracking. It only says what the answer form looks like.

sections.title: The Tracking Status Notification
sections.content:
A Message Tracking Status Notification (MTSN) is returned as the body of a tracking request. The body MUST be a multipart/related with type parameter message/tracking-status, and each subpart MUST be of type message/tracking-status. There can be several parts when an MTQP server chains the request to the next server.

The content type has no optional parameters. The 7bit encoding is sufficient and MUST be used so that it stays readable in non-MIME mail readers.

The body is modeled after RFC 3464. It is a set of fields formatted like RFC 2822 header fields: the per-message fields come first, then a blank line, then one or more groups of per-recipient fields, each group preceded by a blank line.

tracking-status-content =
    per-message-fields 1*( CRLF per-recipient-fields )
sections.eli5: The answer is a short form. The top part is about the whole letter, and below it is one block for each person it was addressed to.

sections.title: Per-Message Fields
sections.content:
Per-message fields apply to every address in one envelope and may appear at most once. They correlate the notification with the original transaction. Three are REQUIRED, each defined as in RFC 3464:

  • Original-Envelope-Id, matching the ENVID used when the message was sent.
  • Reporting-MTA, the MTA giving the report.
  • Arrival-Date, when the message arrived.

Any number of extension fields may follow.
sections.eli5: The top of the form says which letter this is, who is answering, and when the letter arrived.

sections.title: Per-Recipient Fields
sections.content:
Each recipient gets a group of contiguous fields. Original-Recipient, Final-Recipient, Action and Status are REQUIRED. Remote-MTA, Last-Attempt-Date and Will-Retry-Until are optional in the grammar, with extra rules:

  • Remote-MTA MUST NOT be included if no delivery attempt was made or the Action is opaque.
  • Last-Attempt-Date is REQUIRED if any attempt has been made and the Action is not opaque, and MUST NOT be included if no attempt was made.
  • Will-Retry-Until MUST NOT be included if the message is not in the local queue or the Action is opaque; otherwise it SHOULD be included.

The Status field is as in RFC 3464, with one new code added to RFC 3463: X.1.9, message relayed to non-compliant mailer. A 2.1.9 status MUST be used only with a relayed action.
sections.eli5: Each person on the letter gets their own block saying what happened, with extra lines only when they make sense, such as a last try time only if a try happened.

sections.title: The Action Values
sections.content:
The REQUIRED Action field says what the Reporting-MTA did with the message for this recipient. There are seven valid values:

  • failed: could not be delivered; if DSNs are enabled a failed DSN should already have been returned.
  • delayed: waiting in the MTA queue. Essentially, the message is located and it is here.
  • delivered: delivered to the final recipient, including delivery to a mailing list exploder. It does not mean the message was read. The tracking agent SHOULD NOT track further downstream.
  • expanded: delivered to the specified address and forwarded to multiple additional addresses that are not trackable. No further downstream requests.
  • relayed: delivered into an environment that does not support tracking. No further downstream requests.
  • transferred: passed to another MTRK-compliant MTA. The tracking agent SHOULD attempt further downstream requests unless a chaining response already gave that information.
  • opaque: the message may or may not have been seen by this system, and no further information is available.

To choose between expanded and delivered, use expanded whenever the MTA knows the message goes to multiple addresses. If delivery goes to a program that might expand a list without the MTA knowing, and the MTA cannot ensure it will, it should say delivered.

A message handed to a Local Delivery Agent that understands tracking, such as one speaking LMTP with MTRK, SHOULD have the request passed on. The report for that step looks like a transfer to a compliant MTA: transferred.
sections.eli5: The answer is one of seven simple words, such as 'lost', 'waiting here', 'handed over' or 'passed to someone else, ask them'. Some words mean stop asking, and one means keep following the trail.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Malicious servers might try to subvert tracking and return false information, which could cause misdirection or misinterpretation of results.

Confidentiality is the other concern. A recipient may autoforward mail without wanting to reveal the destination address, for example a pager or wireless mailbox. MTA authors are encouraged to let the user keep a forwarding address private, either by answering relayed and disabling further tracking, or by declaring the message delivered, re-sending it to the hidden address and disabling further tracking.

Tracking algorithms MUST NOT track through list expansions. For a message delivered to a list, the response MUST be expanded and MUST NOT show the list contents.
sections.eli5: Someone could lie in their answer, so be a little careful. And some people do not want you to learn where their mail goes next, so the form can stop the trail there.

items.label: Not delivered
items.desc: The message could not be delivered.

items.label: In the queue
items.desc: Waiting in the MTA queue for future delivery.

items.label: Final delivery
items.desc: Delivered to the final recipient; do not track further.

items.label: Left tracking
items.desc: Passed to an environment without tracking support.

items.label: Unknown
items.desc: May or may not have been seen; no more information.
